thread.title: Buy Google Because Gmail, Maps More Useful Than Facebook: Analyst

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Buy Google Because Gmail, Maps More Useful Than Facebook: Analyst
text:
Google consumer products — such as Gmail and maps — have more staying power than Facebook 's ( FB ) social media features, says one Wall Street analyst who upgraded Alphabet ( GOOGL ) to buy following a post-earnings sell-off.
X "Alphabet's products seem to have more proven durability and utility in the lives of consumers than Facebook's products, as displayed in recent weakness of users and usage in Facebook's most mature and highly monetized market of North America," Stifel analyst Scott Devitt said in a note to clients. Google on Wednesday released an update of a redesigned Gmail in the wake of its Tuesday earnings report.
Devitt also says Google may weather the current regulatory storm over privacy issues better than Facebook. Analysts expect Facebook management to comment on data privacy issues that have sparked regulatory scrutiny, when it reports earnings late Wednesday.
"The difference in the business models has led Google management to take a more serious approach to the security and privacy of consumers than has been the case at Facebook," he added. Devitt set a price target of 1,234 a share on Google stock.

Google stock fell 4.7% to 1,022 on Tuesday after the internet search giant reported first-quarter results that topped views. But higher spending and lower margins spooked investors. Google edged up a fraction to close at 1,022.99 on the stock market today .
Google, Facebook Regulatory Risk The company said first-quarter earnings were $13.33 a share, including investment gains on equity securities, up 72% from a year ago. Excluding the gain, profits amounted to $9.93 per share, still topping consensus estimates. Revenue jumped 26% to $31.15 billion.
Adjusted operating margins were 40.6%, below analyst projections for 41.9%. Capital spending jumped to $7.3 billion from $2.5 billion in the year-ago period, including $2.4 billion for a real estate purchase in Manhattan.
"We do believe Alphabet is competing from behind with the likes of Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ), and Microsoft ( MSFT ) in the areas of mobile hardware, online shopping, home devices, and cloud," Devitt said. "However, long-term success in any or multiple of these areas isn't necessary for the stock to work from current levels."
